9 Habits of People Who Stay Fit

How many people find these to be true? My biggest problem is sleep. With a 45 hour work week, two kids, a wife, it is hard to find time to work out, sleep and keep in the work game. Now that I think about it, I think my problem is more of a time management thing. But if I get a day where I work out, go to work, spend time with my family, and work on my career I only get 4 or five hours and then I am spent for the next day or two.

I have trouble with sleep as well.

So a 45 hour week meaning you work 9 hours a day (5 days week)?

Unless the 9 hour day is your choice, I'd have a word with your employer. If you feel that your work is taking too much of your life away from you, I'd reconsider your job.

It's really a personal decision. How much time do you want to spend on getting fit vs. how much time do you want to spend doing other things?

You may want to make habitual changes. How do you commute to work? I cycle every day. A few people I work with also do this. But where it saves on fuel or transport costs, you spend more on food. If you're eating right, this won't be an issue. It will be tough to start but will get easier with time. (Not a week nor a month, this is in the time scale of 3-6 months or something.) My brother commutes 15 miles by bike to work, I know someone else that commutes 20 to theirs. I commute about 5 miles by Mountain bike, for anything above 10, I'd recommend either a Hybrid or a Road bike.

You could join a social community, not online like Voat but at the gym like a Martial Arts group. Chat with them and make friends or bring a friend with you. Once you have friends there it's a lot harder to quit as you'll be letting them down.

Get your family involved. Go to something like Climbing. If your family is not as active then maybe consider doing something like a trail hike on a weekend or I don't know what you consider a reasonable level of activeness.

The important part I want to get over is that if you think you can't handle gym and work and family, then try and get them involved. You don't NEED to go to the gym to be fit, the gym is just a place with a lot of machines to help you get fit.

I also feel it is important to mention rest days are important. As long as you put in some work and then rest and recover, then some more.
